assumptions: A rigid PLA/PETG-like print on a level hard surface is the intended use case.
The circular track center is above the computed solid center of mass and horizontally aligned within 3 mm for static restoring intent.
The back-face print stance avoids support material; shallow front relief faces upward.

components.form: Flat-print 2.5D fused fox masses inside a thick curled-tail silhouette with a circular convex lower track and rounded C-shaped through-window moon.
components.interfaces: No assembly interfaces; broad 24 mm contact across the desk and one-handed side nudge.
components.name: Fox, tail track, and crescent window
components.placement: Silhouette in XY, 24 mm extrusion along Z, flat back on Z=0 for printing, lower tail tangent on Y=0 for use.
components.purpose: Recognizable sleeping-fox silhouette and complete gravity rocking interaction in one print.

concept.intended_interaction: Place the fox upright on its tail arc, nudge either side gently, watch the nose chase the tail through a small decaying rock, and allow the low center of mass to return the crescent window upright.
concept.signature_decision: The visible tail and functional contact path are the same 40 mm-radius arc; the crescent is a through-window rather than decoration.
concept.summary: A monolithic side-profile sleeping fox: its oversized curled tail is a circular rocker track, its nose almost meets the tail tip, and a true crescent aperture returns upright after a small gravity-driven chase.
concept.title: Moonchase Fox
unresolved_risks: Digital geometry cannot prove real damping, friction, rocking duration, durability, or human delight.
Very soft or uneven desk surfaces may mute the tiny chase.
Actual FDM shrink and first-layer elephant foot can slightly alter the contact arc.

research.dimension_basis: Palm scale was set to roughly 100 x 80 x 24 mm; 24 mm width creates a broad stance, the 40 mm track radius makes a slow small-angle response, and the 11 mm radial tail floor exceeds the 0.8 mm two-line wall minimum for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
research.evidence_boundary: These checks establish digital geometry and static restoring intent only; no physical print or human playtest is claimed.
research.evidence_plan: Generate canonical STEP/STL, assert one solid, inspect topology and bounds, verify bed datum, compute center of mass against the track center, run watertight/manifold mesh and thickness gates, and inspect an exact-STL chromatic render.
research.method: Wish-driven parametric design using the selected Pico Press geometry/balance method; no external components or reference images are required.

motion_families_compared.reason: Constant curvature, broad one-piece load path, predictable gravity return, and the track can remain the visible tail.
Changing curvature gives a more abrupt response and makes a clean center-of-mass criterion less legible.
Harder reversal and visible feet weaken the sleeping curled silhouette.
